rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.ne: 3.7 हेरचाहकर्ताको मानसिक स्वास्थ्य तथा मनोसामाजिक कल्याण प्रवर्द्धन गर्ने र बालबालिकालाई सहयोग गर्ने उनीहरूको क्षमता सुदृढ गर्ने
rows.bt: 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.note: Reuses the supplied activity label verbatim as an unreviewed candidate.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: Children who grow up in a safe, loving, responsive and caregiving environment tend to be more emotionally secure, socially competent and better able to cope with adversity.
rows.ne: सुरक्षित, मायालु, आवश्यकताप्रति उत्तरदायी र हेरचाह प्रदान गर्ने वातावरणमा हुर्केका बालबालिका भावनात्मक रूपमा बढी सुरक्षित, सामाजिक रूपमा बढी सक्षम र प्रतिकूल परिस्थितिको सामना गर्न बढी समर्थ हुने प्रवृत्ति हुन्छ।
rows.bt: Children who grow up in a safe, loving environment that is responsive to their needs and provides care tend to be more emotionally secure, more socially capable and more able to cope with adverse circumstances.
rows.note: Describes everyday caregiving and developmental functioning, not a clinical diagnosis.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: Emergencies can severely disrupt caregivers’53 abilities to provide nurturing care54 and undermine their well-being by introducing risk factors such as economic insecurity, social upheaval and extreme stress.
rows.ne: आपत्कालीन अवस्थाले आर्थिक असुरक्षा, सामाजिक उथलपुथल र चरम तनाव जस्ता जोखिमका कारक उत्पन्न गरेर हेरचाहकर्ताहरूको53 बाल विकासलाई पोषण गर्ने स्याहार54 प्रदान गर्ने क्षमतामा गम्भीर अवरोध पुर्‍याउन र उनीहरूको कल्याणमा ह्रास ल्याउन सक्छ।
rows.bt: Emergency situations can, by generating risk factors such as economic insecurity, social upheaval and extreme stress, seriously obstruct the ability of caregivers53 to provide care54 that nurtures child development and cause a decline in their well-being.
rows.note: The draft preserves possibility, caregiver scope and footnote markers 53 and 54.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: Integrated activities can support caregivers to look after their own physical and mental health needs and promote positive caregiving skills.
rows.ne: एकीकृत गतिविधिहरूले हेरचाहकर्तालाई आफ्नै शारीरिक तथा मानसिक स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी आवश्यकताको ख्याल राख्न सहयोग गर्न र सकारात्मक हेरचाहका सीपहरू प्रवर्द्धन गर्न सक्छन्।
rows.bt: Integrated activities can help caregivers attend to their own physical and mental health needs and promote positive caregiving skills.
rows.note: Positive caregiving is absent from the glossary; a nonclinical proposal is listed. The supplied mental-health wording remains an unreviewed candidate.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: MHPSS activities for caregivers should build on existing positive family relationships, roles and traditions.
rows.ne: हेरचाहकर्ताका लागि सञ्चालन गरिने MHPSS गतिविधिहरू विद्यमान सकारात्मक पारिवारिक सम्बन्ध, भूमिका र परम्परामा आधारित हुनुपर्छ।
rows.bt: MHPSS activities conducted for caregivers should be based on existing positive family relationships, roles and traditions.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: While women and girls constitute the majority of caregivers, it is also important to consider male caregivers and to acknowledge the roles that siblings and grandparents often play in providing care.
rows.ne: हेरचाहकर्तामध्ये अधिकांश महिला र बालिका भए पनि पुरुष हेरचाहकर्तालाई पनि ध्यानमा राख्नु र हेरचाह प्रदान गर्न दाजुभाइ-दिदीबहिनी तथा हजुरबुबा-हजुरआमाले प्रायः निर्वाह गर्ने भूमिकालाई स्वीकार गर्नु महत्त्वपूर्ण हुन्छ।
rows.bt: Although most caregivers are women and girls, it is important also to take male caregivers into account and to acknowledge the role that brothers and sisters and grandfathers and grandmothers often play in providing care.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: MHPSS activities for caregivers can also be helpful in strengthening social support networks and should prioritize access and inclusion of at-risk caregivers (see Overview, “How can groups and persons at increased risk be prioritized and reached with MHPSS MSP activities and services?” and Resources on MHPSS for at-risk groups on the MHPSS MSP web platform).
rows.ne: हेरचाहकर्ताका लागि सञ्चालन गरिने MHPSS गतिविधिहरू सामाजिक सहयोग सञ्जाल सुदृढ गर्न पनि उपयोगी हुन सक्छन् र यी गतिविधिहरूले जोखिममा रहेका हेरचाहकर्ताको पहुँच र समावेशितालाई प्राथमिकता दिनुपर्छ (झलक अन्तर्गतको “बढी जोखिममा रहेका समूह र व्यक्तिहरूलाई कसरी प्राथमिकता दिन र उनीहरूसम्म MHPSS MSP गतिविधि र सेवाहरू पुर्‍याउन सकिन्छ?” तथा MHPSS MSP वेब प्लेटफर्ममा जोखिममा रहेका समूहका लागि MHPSS सम्बन्धी स्रोत सामग्री हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: MHPSS activities conducted for caregivers may also be useful for strengthening social support networks, and these activities should prioritize access and inclusion for caregivers at risk (see “How can groups and individuals at greater risk be prioritized and MHPSS MSP activities and services be brought to them?” under the overview, and resource materials on MHPSS for groups at risk on the MHPSS MSP web platform).
rows.note: Social support networks is absent from the glossary; a nonclinical proposal is listed.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: 53 In this section, “caregivers” refers to those with parental responsibilities, regardless of whether or not they are the biological or legal parents of the children in their care. Particular care should be taken to support caregivers who are themselves children.
rows.ne: 53 यस खण्डमा “हेरचाहकर्ता” भन्नाले आफ्नो हेरचाहमा रहेका बालबालिकाका जैविक वा कानुनी अभिभावक भए वा नभए पनि अभिभावकीय जिम्मेवारी भएका व्यक्तिलाई जनाउँछ। आफैँ बालबालिका रहेका हेरचाहकर्तालाई सहयोग गर्न विशेष ध्यान दिनुपर्छ।
rows.bt: 53 In this section, “caregiver” refers to a person with parental responsibilities, whether or not they are the biological or legal parent of the children in their care. Special attention should be given to supporting caregivers who are themselves children.
rows.note: General safety guidance concerning caregivers who are themselves children; review pending.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: 54 Nurturing care involves responsive, affectionate, emotionally supportive caregiving that protects children against threats, provides opportunities for learning and meets the child’s health, security and nutritional needs.
rows.ne: 54 बाल विकासलाई पोषण गर्ने स्याहारमा बालबालिकाका आवश्यकताप्रति उत्तरदायी, स्नेहपूर्ण र भावनात्मक सहयोग प्रदान गर्ने हेरचाह समावेश हुन्छ, जसले बालबालिकालाई खतराबाट जोगाउँछ, सिकाइका अवसर प्रदान गर्छ र उनीहरूको स्वास्थ्य, सुरक्षा तथा पोषणसम्बन्धी आवश्यकता पूरा गर्छ।
rows.bt: 54 Care that nurtures child development includes care that is responsive to children’s needs, affectionate and emotionally supportive, which protects children from danger, provides learning opportunities and meets their health, safety and nutrition needs.
rows.note: The definition concerns ordinary caregiving, not a clinical intervention.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: Identify opportunities for integrated caregiver activities (e.g. in health, education, child protection or nutrition programmes).
rows.ne: हेरचाहकर्ताका लागि एकीकृत गतिविधि सञ्चालन गर्ने अवसरहरू पहिचान गर्नुहोस् (जस्तै, स्वास्थ्य, शिक्षा, बाल संरक्षण वा पोषण कार्यक्रमहरूमा)।
rows.bt: Identify opportunities to conduct integrated activities for caregivers (for example, in health, education, child protection or nutrition programmes).

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: Assess the needs and priorities of caregivers to inform the development of materials and planning of activities.
rows.ne: सामग्री विकास र गतिविधिको योजनालाई दिशा दिन हेरचाहकर्ताका आवश्यकता र प्राथमिकताको लेखाजोखा गर्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: Assess caregivers’ needs and priorities to guide material development and activity planning.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: Develop/select, adapt and translate orientation, skills training and IEC materials on caregiver self-care (e.g. stress management and coping skills), positive caregiving, child development and supporting children in distress, (see the recommended training topics for building caregiver skills in child development, positive caregiving and supporting children in distress on the MHPSS MSP web platform).
rows.ne: हेरचाहकर्ताको स्वहेरचाह (जस्तै तनाव व्यवस्थापन र कठिनाइको सामना गर्ने सीप), सकारात्मक हेरचाह, बाल विकास र व्यथामा रहेका बालबालिकालाई सहयोग गर्ने विषयमा अभिमुखीकरणका सामग्री, सीपसम्बन्धी तालिमका सामग्री र IEC सामग्री विकास/छनोट गर्नुहोस्, अनुकूलन गर्नुहोस् र अनुवाद गर्नुहोस् (बाल विकास, सकारात्मक हेरचाह र व्यथामा रहेका बालबालिकालाई सहयोग गर्ने विषयमा हेरचाहकर्ताका सीप विकास गर्नका लागि सिफारिस गरिएका तालिमका विषयहरू MHPSS MSP वेब प्लेटफर्ममा हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: Develop/select, adapt and translate orientation materials, skills training materials and IEC materials on caregiver self-care (such as stress management and skills for coping with difficulties), positive care, child development and supporting children in distress (see the recommended training topics for developing caregivers' skills in child development, positive care and supporting children in distress on the MHPSS MSP web platform).
rows.note: Stress management and coping skills are retained as general self-care content rather than named therapies; IEC, MHPSS and MSP are preserved.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: Train facilitators to provide orientations, capacity-building and supportive follow-up to caregivers (see the recommended MHPSS training topics for workers providing activities that build MHPSS capacity and support well-being among caregivers and teachers on the MHPSS MSP web platform).
rows.ne: हेरचाहकर्तालाई अभिमुखीकरण, क्षमता विकास र सहयोगात्मक अनुवर्ती सहयोग प्रदान गर्न सहजकर्तालाई तालिम दिनुहोस् (हेरचाहकर्ता र शिक्षकको MHPSS क्षमता विकास गर्ने तथा उनीहरूको कल्याणमा सहयोग गर्ने गतिविधि सञ्चालन गर्ने कार्यकर्ताका लागि सिफारिस गरिएका MHPSS सम्बन्धी तालिमका विषयहरू MHPSS MSP वेब प्लेटफर्ममा हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: Train facilitators to provide orientation, capacity development and supportive follow-up assistance to caregivers (see the recommended MHPSS training topics on the MHPSS MSP web platform for workers conducting activities to develop caregivers’ and teachers’ MHPSS capacity and support their well-being).
rows.note: Well-being is used here as a general programme outcome, not a clinical term; a proposal is listed.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: Provide orientations and/or skills training to caregivers on positive caregiving, child development, supporting children in distress and on self-care. Include caregivers of children with disabilities and children with specific protection vulnerabilities (e.g. children with developmental disabilities, children associated with armed forces and armed groups, child survivors of sexual violence or GBV; see key considerations 25 and 34).
rows.ne: हेरचाहकर्ताहरूलाई सकारात्मक हेरचाह, बाल विकास, व्यथामा रहेका बालबालिकालाई सहयोग गर्ने र स्वहेरचाहका विषयमा अभिमुखीकरण र/वा सीपसम्बन्धी तालिम प्रदान गर्नुहोस्। अपाङ्गता भएका बालबालिका र संरक्षणसम्बन्धी विशेष जोखिममा रहेका बालबालिकाका हेरचाहकर्ताहरूलाई समावेश गर्नुहोस् (जस्तै विकाससम्बन्धी अपाङ्गता भएका बालबालिका, सशस्त्र बल र सशस्त्र समूहसँग सम्बन्धित बालबालिका, यौन हिंसा वा GBV का प्रभावित व्यक्तिहरूमा पर्ने बालबालिका; मुख्य विचारणीय पक्षहरू 25 र 34 हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: Provide caregivers with orientation and/or skills training on positive care, child development, supporting children in distress and self-care. Include caregivers of children with disabilities and children at particular protection-related risk (such as children with developmental disabilities, children associated with armed forces and armed groups, children who are among persons affected by sexual violence or GBV; see key considerations 25 and 34).
rows.note: The frozen label प्रभावित व्यक्तिहरू means affected persons and can include indirectly affected people, whereas survivors denotes people who directly experienced and survived the violence; the source refers specifically to child survivors, not indirectly affected children. bt-divergence: The frozen label प्रभावित व्यक्तिहरू means affected persons, potentially including indirectly affected people, whereas the source specifies children who directly experienced and survived sexual violence or GBV. The frozen form is retained unchanged.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: Facilitate access to a safe space in which to conduct activities as needed.
rows.ne: आवश्यकताअनुसार गतिविधि सञ्चालन गर्न सुरक्षित स्थलमा पहुँच सहज बनाउनुहोस्।
rows.bt: Facilitate access to a safe venue to conduct activities as needed.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: Engage staff with MHPSS technical expertise to oversee activities and provide ongoing supervision to facilitators (e.g. ensuring that activities promote well-being and do not cause harm).
rows.ne: गतिविधिहरूको रेखदेख गर्न र सहजकर्तालाई निरन्तर सुपरिवेक्षण प्रदान गर्न MHPSS सम्बन्धी प्राविधिक विशेषज्ञता भएका कर्मचारीलाई संलग्न गराउनुहोस् (जस्तै, गतिविधिहरूले कल्याण प्रवर्द्धन गर्ने र हानि नगर्ने सुनिश्चित गर्न)।
rows.bt: Engage personnel with technical expertise in MHPSS to oversee activities and provide ongoing supervision to facilitators (for example, to ensure that activities promote well-being and do no harm).
rows.note: General harm-prevention guidance; review pending. Well-being is used as a general programme outcome; a proposal is listed.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: Facilitate referrals for caregivers and other family members to access any needed services and supports (e.g. social services, mental health services, health, protection and education services).
rows.ne: हेरचाहकर्ता र परिवारका अन्य सदस्यलाई आवश्यक पर्ने कुनै पनि सेवा र सहयोगमा पहुँच दिलाउन सम्बन्धित सेवामा पठाउने कार्य सहज बनाउनुहोस् (जस्तै, सामाजिक सेवा, मानसिक स्वास्थ्य सेवा तथा स्वास्थ्य, संरक्षण र शिक्षा सम्बन्धी सेवा)।
rows.bt: Facilitate referral to relevant services to enable caregivers and other family members to access any services and support they need (for example, social services, mental health services and services related to health, protection and education).
rows.note: General service-access guidance; review pending. The mental-health service wording reuses wording supplied in activity 3.10 and remains unreviewed.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: Additional actions for consideration (depending on context and available resources)
rows.ne: विचार गर्नका लागि दिइएका थप कार्यहरू (सन्दर्भ र उपलब्ध स्रोतहरूका आधारमा)
rows.bt: Additional actions provided for consideration (depending on the context and available resources)

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: Promote support networks for caregivers by establishing or strengthening social groups, peer-to-peer support groups, play groups and self-help groups (see MSP activity 3.4).
rows.ne: सामाजिक समूह, समकक्षीबीच सहयोग आदानप्रदान गर्ने समूह, खेल समूह र स्वसहयोग समूह स्थापना वा सुदृढ गरेर हेरचाहकर्ताका लागि सहयोग सञ्जाल प्रवर्द्धन गर्नुहोस् (MSP गतिविधि 3.4 हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: Promote support networks for caregivers by establishing or strengthening social groups, groups for exchanging support among peers, play groups and self-help groups (see MSP activity 3.4).
rows.note: These are ordinary community-group arrangements, not named clinical interventions.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: Provide structured group MHPSS interventions to caregivers.
rows.ne: हेरचाहकर्ताहरूलाई समूहमा सञ्चालन गरिने संरचित MHPSS हस्तक्षेपहरू प्रदान गर्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: Provide caregivers with structured MHPSS interventions conducted in groups.
rows.note: The draft retains interventions, the structured group format and MHPSS without substituting generic activities. The draft and BT attach 'structured' to the groups rather than to the group MHPSS interventions. The repair makes the interventions structured while retaining group delivery and caregivers as recipients.

rows.en: Key consideration 25: Supporting caregivers when a child has been sexually abused
rows.ne: मुख्य विचारणीय पक्ष 25: बालबालिकामाथि यौन दुर्व्यवहार भएको अवस्थामा हेरचाहकर्तालाई सहयोग गर्ने
rows.bt: Key consideration 25: Supporting caregivers when children have been sexually abused
rows.note: General safeguarding topic heading, not a verbatim safeguarding declaration; review pending.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: When a child has been sexually abused, their non-offending caregivers may feel anger, disbelief, worry, guilt, shame, sadness and fear. These emotions can interfere with their ability to provide the child with the support, care, and attention they need.
rows.ne: बालबालिकामाथि यौन दुर्व्यवहार भएको अवस्थामा दुर्व्यवहारमा संलग्न नभएका हेरचाहकर्ताले रिस, अविश्वास, चिन्ता, दोषबोध, लाज, दुःख र डर अनुभव गर्न सक्छन्। यी भावनाले बालबालिकालाई आवश्यक सहयोग, हेरचाह र ध्यान प्रदान गर्ने उनीहरूको क्षमतामा बाधा पुर्‍याउन सक्छन्।
rows.bt: When children have been sexually abused, caregivers who were not involved in the abuse may experience anger, disbelief, anxiety, guilt, shame, sadness and fear. These feelings may hinder their ability to provide children with the support, care and attention they need.
rows.note: The emotions are ordinary descriptions, not diagnostic terms. General safeguarding guidance; review pending. Non-offending caregivers is absent from the glossary; a proposal is listed.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.7 Promote caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial well-being and strengthen their capacity to support children
rows.en: Non-offending caregivers should be offered emotional support, basic education about sexual abuse, and information on how to support the child in dealing with the emotional, social, and physical consequences of abuse. For information on how to provide this support, see UNICEF and IRC (2012). Caring for Child Survivors of Sexual Abuse Guidelines and Training Package.
rows.ne: दुर्व्यवहारमा संलग्न नभएका हेरचाहकर्तालाई भावनात्मक सहयोग, यौन दुर्व्यवहारबारे आधारभूत शिक्षा र दुर्व्यवहारका भावनात्मक, सामाजिक तथा शारीरिक परिणामको सामना गर्न बालबालिकालाई कसरी सहयोग गर्ने भन्ने जानकारी उपलब्ध गराउने प्रस्ताव गर्नुपर्छ। यस्तो सहयोग कसरी प्रदान गर्ने भन्ने जानकारीका लागि UNICEF र IRC (2012) को Caring for Child Survivors of Sexual Abuse Guidelines and Training Package हेर्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: An offer must be made to provide caregivers who were not involved in the abuse with emotional support, basic education about sexual abuse, and information on how to help children cope with the emotional, social and physical consequences of abuse. For information on how to provide such support, see UNICEF and IRC (2012), Caring for Child Survivors of Sexual Abuse Guidelines and Training Package.
rows.note: General safeguarding guidance, not a verbatim declaration; review pending. The publication title is retained in English. Non-offending caregivers is absent from the glossary; a proposal is listed. The source says support, education and information should be offered; the Nepali and back-translation instead say they should be provided. The revision restores offering rather than presuming receipt. The back-translation strengthens the obligation from support, education, and information that “should be offered” to an offer that “must be made.”
